newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S.-Kuwait chemical venture signs $1.2 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Kuwait chemical venture signs $1.2 bln loan.

text.p: A group of Western, Asian and Arab banks on Sunday agreed to lend $1.2 billion to a U.S.-Kuwaiti joint venture to build a large petrochemical complex in the Gulf state, an official statement said.

Equate, a venture between America's Union Carbide Corp, Kuwait's Petrochemical Industries Company and Kuwait's Bubiyan Petrochemical Company, signed the loan agreement with a syndicate of over 50 banks at a ceremony in Kuwait, the statement said.
Bankers have called the loan the largest non-recourse financing ever arranged in the Gulf outside of the Gulf's crude oil and refinery sector.
It is also the first major loan in the region to incorporate a mixture of conventional and Islamic financing, they said.
The total project cost is $2 billion. The non-debt portion will come from the partners' equity participation.

The statement said the loan was arranged by Arab Banking Corporation, Saudi-based Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation (APICORP), Chase Manhattan Bank, Citibank, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank GIOH.BH, Kuwait-based Gulf Investment Corporation (GIC), JP Morgan, Kuwait Finance House and National Bank of Kuwait.
These banks will also underwtrite the loan with al-Ahli Bank of Kuwait, Saudi-based Arab Investment Company, Burgan Bank, Commercial Bank of Kuwait and Gulf Bank of Kuwait, the statement said.
The loan has two tranches -- $500 million over 10-1/2 years for Kuwaiti institutions and $700 million over 8-1/2 years for Gulf-based and international institutions.
